objective: Unify requirement and architecture table action columns with the repository's latest primary, frequent and more-action hierarchy while removing excessive fixed-column whitespace.
users: Requirement users reviewing records, advancing stages and maintaining requirement data
Architecture users viewing, editing and deleting logical or physical subsystems

requirements.statement: Requirement difference rows must keep record and review actions visible, keep submit-review visible when eligible, and move edit and delete into a more-actions menu.
acceptance: Change history is always visible and approval history is visible only when a workflow instance exists
Submit review is directly visible only for pending or returned rows
Edit and delete retain canEditDiff visibility and invoke their existing handlers from the more menu
The fixed action column is no wider than 280 pixels
counterexample: Reviewed rows retain a 380-pixel mostly empty action column
Edit or delete becomes available for a non-editable row
Submit review is hidden inside a low-frequency menu

requirements.statement: Legacy requirement and system catalog rows must separate frequent actions from low-frequency or destructive actions without changing behavior.
acceptance: Legacy rows show stage advance and change history directly and place stage history, edit and delete in more actions
System rows show edit directly and place delete in more actions
Existing handlers, confirmations and error messages remain in use
requirements.source: Approved option 1 and existing delivery-showcase hierarchy.
counterexample: All five legacy actions remain flat in one row
Delete loses its confirmation or permission condition

requirements.statement: Logical and physical subsystem tables must use the same detail, edit and more-actions presentation with standard icons and spacing.
acceptance: Detail is always visible with a view icon
Edit is visible only with canUpdate and uses an edit icon
More is visible only with delete permission and contains the existing delete command
Desktop and mobile labels and icon semantics remain consistent
requirements.source: User requested both merged branches to follow current common styles.
counterexample: The two architecture pages use different action markup

requirements.statement: Action containers must remain compact, non-wrapping and readable across fixed-column scrolling, themes and required desktop/mobile viewports.
acceptance: Adjacent Element Plus buttons have stable gaps and no inherited left margin
UiDataTable continues to own fixed-column background, shadow and hover behavior
The 1280x800 desktop viewport has no clipped action labels or excessive action-column whitespace
The 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 viewports have no page-level horizontal overflow and architecture mobile cards expose reachable actions
requirements.source: design-h5.md and frontend UI integration contract.
counterexample: Buttons wrap to two lines in one row
Fixed-column content becomes transparent during horizontal scrolling
The page width exceeds the mobile viewport

invariants: No backend, API, database, permission or audit behavior changes
Every action retains its existing visibility condition, confirmation and handler
No business handler is added or modified; dropdown entries only invoke existing handlers
UiDataTable remains the owner of fixed-column foundation styles
No new dependency or public UI component is introduced
constraints: Use Vue 3, TypeScript, Element Plus and existing semantic theme variables
Modify only the requirement page, architecture module pages, architecture local CSS and current-task governance artifacts
Do not modify web/src/components/ui or web/src/styles.css
Implementation requires a ready requirement scope and a separately approved implementation plan
non_goals: Refactoring the complete requirement management page
Adding complete mobile card lists to requirement management
Migrating action columns in unrelated modules
Changing workflow, stage or deletion behavior

selected_approach.name: Module-local primary, frequent and more-action hierarchy
selected_approach.reason: It directly reuses the delivery showcase interaction pattern, fixes excessive width and flat action lists, and avoids broad public-component regression.

alternatives.name: Width-only adjustment
alternatives.rejected_because: Rows with many eligible actions would still wrap or crowd and the hierarchy problem would remain.

alternatives.name: New shared UiTableActions component
alternatives.rejected_because: It would require a public frontend capability change and regression across unrelated modules.

inside: Requirement difference, legacy requirement and system catalog action columns
Logical and physical subsystem desktop and mobile action presentation
Module-local action spacing and responsive styles
Frontend build and browser viewport verification
outside: Backend services, APIs, database and permissions
Shared UI components and global styles

components.name: RequirementsView
components.responsibility: Reorder requirement actions, route low-frequency actions through dropdown commands and provide local compact action styles.

components.name: LogicalSubsystemPage
components.responsibility: Render standard detail, edit and more actions for logical subsystems.

components.name: PhysicalSubsystemPage
components.responsibility: Render the same standard action structure for physical subsystems.

components.name: architecture.css
components.responsibility: Apply module-local non-wrapping action spacing without duplicating fixed-column foundation styles.

interfaces.name: Existing UI action handlers
interfaces.contract: Moving an action into a dropdown changes only its entry point; the same handler, conditions, confirmation and API call remain authoritative.

data_flows.input: Current row state and authenticated frontend permission set
transitions: render eligible low-frequency actions in more menu
data_flows.output: The same business operation with a compact and consistent action presentation

error_handling.behavior: Keep the row state and use the existing handler's error message without optimistic success.
error_handling.recovery: Retry the action or refresh the list.

error_handling.condition: No permission exists for a conditional action
error_handling.behavior: Do not render the action or an empty menu placeholder.
error_handling.recovery: An administrator grants the existing permission; no new permission is introduced.

security: Frontend visibility remains an experience layer and does not replace backend authorization
No identity, permission or request payload changes
performance: No additional request, watcher or dependency
Dropdown rendering is local to the existing row
compatibility: Existing routes, types, APIs and handlers remain compatible
UiDataTable global fixed-column behavior remains unchanged
operations: Pure frontend rollback by reverting the affected page and local CSS files
No migration, configuration or deployment-order dependency

verification_strategy.signal: Every direct and menu action remains visible only in its original state and invokes the original handler.
verification_strategy.method: Static diff inspection plus real browser clicks across representative row states.

verification_strategy.signal: No clipped labels, excessive operation-column whitespace, fixed-column bleed-through or page-level mobile overflow.
verification_strategy.method: Browser screenshots and DOM width checks at 1280x800, 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 in light and dark themes.

verification_strategy.signal: Frontend type checking and production bundling succeed.
verification_strategy.method: npm --prefix web run build and git diff --check.

assumptions.text: The requested optimization is limited to table action presentation and does not require a full requirement-management mobile card redesign.
assumptions.basis: The user explicitly highlighted the operation column and asked both merged branches to follow the latest common style.
assumptions.falsifier: The user requests complete mobile list restructuring or broader page redesign.

decisions.decision: Use module-local action hierarchy and styles without adding a public component.
decisions.reason: Smallest compatible scope with lower regression cost.

decisions.decision: Move low-frequency and destructive actions into more menus while retaining high-frequency actions directly.
decisions.reason: Matches delivery-showcase and design-h5 operation hierarchy.

risks.risk: A row-state combination exposes more direct actions than the selected fixed width supports.
risks.mitigation: Cover pending, returned, in-review and reviewed rows in desktop browser verification before fixing the final width.

risks.risk: A dropdown command is wired to the wrong existing handler.
risks.impact: The user may trigger an unintended action.
risks.mitigation: Use typed command unions and click every migrated menu item in browser verification.

approval.evidence: User reviewed and confirmed design revision 1 on 2026-08-21, then clarified that implementation must only adjust styles and action-entry presentation without changing business logic.
